facts.raw_span: pruritic, pink scaling plaques on her face and neck
lesions subsequently involved her chest, abdomen, and back and flared with sun exposure
Well-demarcated plaques with an overlying scale crust occurring in a photodistributed pattern on the central face, with involvement of chest, abdomen, and back
Antinuclear antibody titers positive at 1:640
Lymphopenia present
Normocytic anemia present
Negative or within normal limits: antiribonucleoprotein, antihistone, antiphospholipid, anti-Smith, anti-Ro/Sjögren syndrome antigen A, and anti-La/Sjögren syndrome antigen B antibodies
Normal C3, C4, CH50, rapid plasma reagin, and creatinine levels
Epidermal acanthosis, spongiosis, and acantholytic keratinocytes
Dense lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate in the dermis, with scattered neutrophils and eosinophils
Granular and linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone and abundant intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 in the upper two-thirds of the epidermis
Previous treatment with hydroxychloroquine sulfate, fluocinonide ointment, 0.05%, and tacrolimus ointment, 0.1% failed to improve the condition

concepts.why: The patient's positive antinuclear antibody titers, epidermal acanthosis, and granular deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone are consistent with lupus erythematosus.
The patient's well-demarcated plaques with an overlying scale crust and photodistributed pattern are characteristic of discoid lupus erythematosus.
The patient's lesions that flared with sun exposure and involved the chest, abdomen, and back are consistent with subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus.
The patient's photodistributed rash and lesions that flared with sun exposure are characteristic of polymorphic light eruption.
The patient's positive antinuclear antibody titers, lymphopenia, and normocytic anemia are consistent with Sjögren's syndrome.
The patient's positive antinuclear antibody titers, lymphopenia, and normal C3 and C4 levels are consistent with rheumatoid arthritis.
The patient's positive antinuclear antibody titers, epidermal acanthosis, and dense lymphoplasmacellular infiltrate are consistent with dermatomyositis.
The patient's positive antinuclear antibody titers, lymphopenia, and normocytic anemia are consistent with mixed connective tissue disease.

rationales.F11: Granular and linear deposition of IgG and C3 at the basement membrane zone is characteristic of lupus erythematosus.
